### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19 and A20 each ran in about half of the cases (roughly 99 and 103 of 200 traces) and were mutually exclusive — they hardly ever appeared in the same trace. In the later window both have nearly vanished, appearing in only 1 and 4 of 200 traces respectively. [OCC001, OCC002, REL009]
- Two activities not observed in any earlier trace, A25 and A26, are executed in about 198 of 200 traces each (about 99 in 100) in the later window. [OCC003, OCC004]
- The new pair occupies the segment the old pair occupied. Earlier, A42 preceded A19 in about 49 in 100 traces and A20 in about 52 in 100, A14 preceded A19/A20 in about half of the traces, and A19/A20 in turn preceded A27 in about half; later, A42 precedes A25 and A26 in about 98 in 100 traces, A14 precedes A25 in about 99 in 100, and A25 and A26 each precede A27 in about 99 in 100. [REL005, REL006, REL012, REL013, REL016, REL017, REL007, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022]
- In the later window A25 and A26 appear together in about 99 in 100 traces, with A25 first in about half and A26 first in about half — no fixed order between them — whereas A19 and A20 were essentially never executed together earlier. [REL018, REL009]
- A42's outgoing transitions moved from mostly A20 (about 42 in 100) and A19 (about 40 in 100) to mostly A25 (about 43 in 100) and A26 (about 41 in 100); the observed gap from A42 to A27 stretched from usually 2 steps (about 82 in 100) to usually 3 steps (about 78 in 100), and A27's average event position moved slightly later in the trace (about 0.41 to 0.43). [DIR008, LAG004, POS005]
- Smaller shifts: A07's follow-up split between A05 and A14 flipped (A05 about 44 to 28 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions, A14 about 26 to 44 in 100), the follow-up profiles of A06 and A10 were redistributed (losing A19/A20 as targets, gaining A25/A26 and others), and the few residual A19/A20 executions are too few to characterise. [DIR002, DIR001, DIR003, OCC001, OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A42/A14 and A27 was restructured by exchanging its activities: earlier, each case executed either A19 or A20 (about half of the cases each, essentially never both) in that position, while in the later window A19 and A20 are nearly never executed and almost every case instead executes both A25 and A26 there, in either order. The support is direct and consistent across indicator families — participation counts, A42's successor profile (about 200 outgoing transitions in each window, moving from A19/A20 to A25/A26), co-occurrence and order relations with A42, A14 and A27 (each backed by about 200 traces in both windows), and the A42-to-A27 distance stretching from about 2 to about 3 steps — and the volume of qualified evidence (43 items against roughly 0.65 expected without a change) far exceeds what random window splits produce. The evidence cannot rule out that A25/A26 are renamed versions of the same steps rather than genuinely new activities, nor determine whether the residual A19/A20 executions (1 and 4 traces) still form an intended rare path. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR008, REL009, REL018, REL020, LAG004]

Other differences: beyond the retargeting towards A25/A26, A06's and A10's follow-up distributions also shifted among other activities (A06 more often leading to A46, A10 more often to A15, A16 and A47), based on moderate numbers of observed transitions (36–48), so these shares are less stable; A07-to-A14 pairs also occur slightly closer together in the later window. [DIR001, DIR003, LAG001]
